text: Almalexia is dead at my hand. The goddess hoped to leave me here dead, and make me a martyr to her new cause. Now, she and Sotha Sil both lie dead in what is left of the Clockwork City. Gestalt appeared before me, and explained his nature; he is a copy of Sotha Sil's mind, partially uploaded into the city. He has offered me the choice of completing this uploading process, or destroying him, leaving the city to die.

I have chosen to save Gestalt and the city. Gestalt, or perhaps now Sotha Sil, thanked me, and gave me his lab and the city to watch over. He requested that, should he ever go mad, I be the one to destroy him permanently.

I have chosen to destroy Gestalt, and by extension the Clockwork City. As he died, he thanked me for releasing him from the binds of life, and gave me his lab, which will still function. He warned me that the city will be dead now, though perhaps it is for the best.

I have returned to Mournhold and been visited by the spirit of the Daedra Azura. She has told me that the death of Almalexia was just, and that it was she, not Sotha Sil, who was mad. The time of the Tribunal, says Azura, is gone. As a sign of her love for the Dunmer, she has ended the ashstorms in Mournhold, and promised they will never return
Rebuilding Fyr Manor

My servant in Fyr Manor has informed me that Fyr Manor is broken. Apparently it had many extra rooms that were lost over the years. These rooms were stored in special keys, that were, again, lost. If I can retrieve these keys and bring them back to Fyr Manor, the rooms will be restored. He does not know how many rooms there are in all.
Flying Trains
Venluen has asked me to find his powered cart, which flew out of his house in the direction of the Temple district a few hours ago.
I have found the powered cart's wreckage. Unfortunately, a priest seems convinced that it is a message from Sotha Sil himself, and wouldn't let me get near it without a fight.
I returned to Venluen, who awkwardly thanked and rewarded me.
I convinced Adaira to see the Foremer.
I convinced Ineriab to see the Foremer.
I convinced Kuteba to see the Foremer.
Role Call
The High Foremer has tasked me with locating and convincing several fabricants to come to their offices and raise the children that they had requested. I am to use force if necessary.
The Foremer thanked me, rather quickly, and rewarded me with some armor and a key.
I convinced Adaira to see the Foremer.
I convinced Ineriab to see the Foremer.
I convinced Kuteba to see the Foremer.
Licherous Intentions
I have agreed to participate in being subjected to several experiments of Favthali. If I survive, I will be payed handsomely.
After being blinded, blown up, poisoned, drained of my strength, and decapitated, Favthali finished his experimentation.
As promised, I was rewarded.
Aquatic Pest Control
Lokan has asked me to kill the slaughterfish infesting the waters beneath his house.
I have killed all the slaughterfish. Lokan rewarded me.
A Lab Rat
I have been kidnapped by a mad wizard, who has placed me and several others in a maze of his own making.
I escaped the maze and killed the wizard.
The Legs of Seht
In my quest to reach the city, I managed to find all six pieces of Sotha Sil's legs. A fabricant in the clockwork city helped me rebuild them into a powerful pair of greaves.

I spoke to a fabricant who told me of six pieces that, when assembled by him, would become a powerful pair of greaves. Unfortunately, these pieces were lost in the outer city, and because I cannot return there, I can never rebuild these greaves.
The Archcanon of Sotha Sil has provided a way for me to come and go between Mundus and the Clockwork City. There is now an active portal in Fyr Manor that will take me to and from the area.
District of the Undead

The Archcanon has told me that the slums, once a peaceful part of the city, have become dangerous, filled with mad fabricants attacking any who enter. He believes that some force in the slums has corrupted them, and that I should attempt to eliminate this force.
The guards at the entrance to the slums have refused to let me in. I should either find a way to gain access, or look for an alternative route.
A fabricant in charge of guarding the slums allowed me to pass through.
I have entered the slums. I should seek out the source of the madness.

At the center of the slums, I entered an ancient vault, presumably used to contain things of interest to Sotha Sil. At the very bottom I discovered a magical monster called the Pocket Cabal, which is the source of the madness in the slums. It now seeks to destroy me and devour my soul.

I have killed the Pocket Cabal, ending the madness in the slums. However because I killed so many fabricants to reach the monster, the residents of this district are furious, and will no longer talk to me.
I have killed the Pocket Cabal, ending the madness in the slums. Because I avoided taking the lives of the innocent but mad fabricants, I am hailed as a merciful hero.
The Roots That Go Deep

The Archcanon has told me that the Arboretum, which supplies the city with flora and fauna, has become sick, and the things within are dying. If I can cure this disease, the district will return to normal. The overseer of the district, the Gardener, will tell me more.

The Gardener has informed me that he knows not of the cause of the disease, but believes that if it is found, it may be destroyed and cured. He has asked me to check three possible sources, a blocked oil flow, an experimental plant that may be contagious, and an old fabricant farm.
I managed to get the oil flowing once more, but there doesn't seem to be any difference.
Despite protests from their owner, I investigate several experiments, but none of them seem to be the source of the disease.
Though I was attacked by the rogue fabricants, they didn't seem to be diseased.

While performing my tasks, a strange presence contacted me. It told me to seek out the core of the Arboretum, located in its lower levels. However, I would have to convince the Gardener to let me into those lower levels, or find my own way in.
The Gardener, though reluctant, gave me the key to the lower arboretum.

In the core of the Arboretum, I spoke with the Tree, a massive intelligence that acts through the Gardener. It has told me that damage to the city wounded the Arboretum, which ultimately became sick from that wound. Seeking to contain it, the Gardener took the infection into himself, and is now unknowingly working to destroy the Arboretum.
The Gardener is now the source of the disease, though he does not know it. I have been tasked by the Tree to either cure him or kill him, ending the infection.
I killed the Gardener, ending the infection at the cost of the District's overseer.
I convinced the Gardener to let me cure him, ending the infection.
Power Corrupts
The Archcanon has told me that the Industrial District has been suffering from power outages. I should speak to the High Foremer in the Industrial District to learn more.
The Foremer was busy, and unhelpful, cryptically mentioning something about generators and fools.
Outside, I met a strange fabricant, who seemed to be interested in helping me, and told me to meet him in his house.

Addamar, the fabricant also investigating the power outages, claims that they begin with surges, and each power surge spikes at certain times. I have been tasked with observing the three largest of these, and finding out from where in the district they begin.

I reported back after discovering the source of each of the largest power surges. Addamar has told me that each of those places requires a large amount of power to keep running, and therefore they are connected. I have now been tasked with finding an old book Addamar once read, a book on power dynamics, which would be in the possession of someone who would have a use for such a thing.

Based on information in the book, Addamar has concluded that some outside force is messing with the central generator of the entire city. Furthermore, the Industrial District may be situated directly over that generator. I have been tasked with investigation the headquarters of the Overclockers, who have had no trouble with power outages.

As it turns out, the Overclockers do seem to know a bit about the power generator, as a miniature one lies in their basement. They admitted that a small group of them recently claimed to have stumbled upon a massive power source, from which they fabricated their own local generator. However, these three Overclockers disappeared a short time ago, presumably to continue fooling with the power core.

Addamar thinks he knows where they have gone, a condemned building on the north side of town, near his house, which may have opened to reveal a passage to the power core, though the house is now sealed and guarded by Watchmen. Luckily, Addamar has given me a tool that will redirect one of the power surges at the Watchmen, disabling them and allowing me to enter the generator room.

I have entered the generator chamber, and confronted the three fabricants. While they seemed generally unaware that they would be destroying the entire city, they nevertheless put up a fight. Unfortunately, the energies of the core overwhelmed all of us, but before I perished I was rescued by the Foremer, who seems now willing to talk to me. It also seems that the power outages have stopped.
Class Warfare

The Archcanon has told me that the Residential District, which lays split between the rich and poor, has recently been facing some conflicts of interest, and fabricants there fight amongst themselves for reasons unknown. I have been tasked to speak to the leader of the Abstemious, the ruling faction there.

Lllolauran-88, their leader, has told me that while there are rich fabricants and poor fabricants, the existence of these classes is more less the result of their own choices in life, and no fabricant naturally feels jealous or above another. However, something seems to be artificially encouraging the recent struggle between the two classes.

For my first task, the Abstemious have found that some fabricants have acquired moon sugar, a substance not usually found in the city. They believe the drugs have in some way indirectly contributed to the struggle. I am to find the source of these drugs. Finding an addict would be a good place to start.
An addicted beggar told me he had gotten his first bits of moon sugar from the brothel in the poor section of the district.

The bartender of the brothel tells me that he has overheard some traders claiming they store their moon sugar in a warehouse on the other side of the district. The warehouse is owned by a man named Relamus.
Relamus denies any action in the moon sugar smuggling, and states that his warehouse is merely rented to other parties. He has given me permission to look around inside.
I found a crate of moon sugar, as well as a note that indicates it belongs to a fabricant named Sehlan.

Sehlan claims guilt in spreading the moon sugar, but knows not where he gets it, and he states that it merely appears at his door every few weeks, but the supply recently stopped. I seem to have reached a dead end, and should return to the Abstemious.

Lllolauran believes that I should pursue another possible line. Recently, someone has been spreading around pamphlets to the rich and poor, encouraging them to turn against each other. I should find who is responsible for such things, and should start by finding a pamphlet.
I was lead to a printer in the Industrial District, who claims that they received an anonymous commission to print the pamphlets. Another dead end. I should return to the Abstemious
Lllolauran has one last possible line for me to pursue, that someone is spreading rumors that indirectly encourage class struggle. I should, once again, find the source of these rumors.

I was attacked by Watchman, who knocked me out and brought me before Relamus. Relamus revealed that he was indeed behind the recent problems. He is also, in fact, a transicant, a mortal man in a fabricant body, and was formerly a high ranking Hlaalu member. He plans to exploit the Clockwork City and then return to Nirn. He then dumped me in a huge pit, leaving me here to die.

Relamus eventually lowered down a terrifying monster called a "Mimic" which took the form of a dwemer machine and attempted to kill me. I defeated it, and escaped on the same lift it was lowered down on. I should confront him and end this once and for all.
I confronted and killed Relamus, who had several rogue Watchmen to help him. The problems in the Residential District should stop now.

But should I call them that? I hesitate to, but fear them nonetheless. My brother and sister know so little, and they will know even less. They will think themselves treading in the footsteps of prophecy, but they're merely tools, a means to an end.
And in time, they will come for me. Perhaps they will have learned by then. Perhaps they will know, that... I am sorry.

When we look at time, we think of it as linear, that exists going from point A, to point B. We fail to understand. Time is water. It flows, and the flow can be redirected. Chronography, the study of time, and events. Those who have it can see the future. The Psijics rejected it, yet still, I practice it. I have peeked into the future, and I have found suffering, and death. The walls between worlds fade, the Red Mountain spews death, and Nerevar Reborn walks the world.

Fabricant skeletal spirits that have bonded together to form one massive construct. In life, these fabricants were usually a family, or a crew that worked together, and they use their teamwork to their advantage. They're fast, deadly, but most importantly they split into their original spirits on death. Bone welders tend to be the larger, stronger types. Explosive fire spells work well against them, I've found.

It isn't enough. City is always expanding, always ticking, but there's too much for me now. Even with my mind I can't process as much information as this. I need workers, helpers. I need something to look after the city.

It is complete. Oceans of oil, fields of ground iron sand, valleys of steel plates, all ticking away, all mine. The quartz works well, and though time passes on a local scale, I can select and immunize that which I do not want to progress.
It is my realm. A perfect clockwork city of my own making.

Light-fractory computing. Brilliant, only really applied for traps originally, but can be made to be far more complex. Simulates a real mind. Emotes, thinks, learns, far greater and far faster than anyone. It is my king, and I am its god. A regent, and his deity.
Still, not enough. City too great, need to delegate. If I make smaller ones, smaller... Intelligences, they could run it. Not any easy task. Would have to make them part of the main system, smaller parts of a greater whole.
A gestalt.
Room online. I have kept it tidy for sir.
It is a lovely view today, sir.

City was attacked today. Not by divines. Travelers, things. I don't know. Came too close, killed too many.
I can't have this. Both things. I have been careless, in emotion and in security. I have spent too long avoiding self-improvement. I am flawed, and from my flaws come a flawed city, which merely leads to disaster. I shall personify these flaws. Give their cancer form and function. My imperfections will guard my city and my person, as they always should have.

I find myself more and more talking to the air. Some might say it was madness. It's not. It's loneliness. 
A deity should look after his people. But I have no people. And so, I will make some. Soul-matrices and construct conjuration is a precise and tested science. Will need machines, workers, have to automate the process. Build them in the image of my beloved dunmer, if need be. 
I'll also need a foundry.

Numidium was powered by the heart of the Missing God. My siblings and I, ascended by means of the same beating jewel. It is the mistake we have all made. To ascend truly, we must not take divinity from the hands of another. 
Thus, my world. A god is as much his realm as it is him. This is yet another mistake we made. For one to become truly a god, truly divine, you must be one with your realm. 
I now know the true purpose of my Regent.

We have been blind, we have been fools. It is an axiom that all mer seek godhood. But we seek it foolishly. The Altmer think that by unbinding the world they will ascend to a form they never had, and we and our dwemer kin were worse. We called ourselves gods, or sought to build ones free from the rule of divine, yet we made the same mistake over and over. We were thieves, taking our divinity from that which we rejected.

The Garden of Akatosh is the sector of manufactory where all life is created. From the great Tree of Flesh the very souls of fabricants grow into eggs, and are sent down the line to the main foundry. In the event that the tree suffers damage, the Clockwork King has created me to advise any travelers on how to repair it.

The cold metal womb of the city, constantly giving birth to new sectors, machines, and intelligences. It is the heart of the city, where the Mystery of Morrowind controls that which controls all. Take care! It is a dangerous area, for creation does not care for little things like you, and the guardians of Sotha Sil will not hesitate to destroy you if you interfere with their purpose.

I keep my word. The city aches no longer, and in time, it will hopefully heal. In return and as promised, I shall show you the way to the Clockwork King's throne. In the center of the lobby of the clocktower now stands a portal. Should you pass through it, you will find yourself in the Underconstruction, from which you may make your way to Sotha Sil.
Be careful though, Nerevar. I cannot tell you what you will find in your journey, but be well prepared, for it will no doubt be difficult.

Though I am restricted in movement, I still hear much of what happens in this city. I can tell you there are pains from the Slums, the Residential District, the Industrial District, the Arboretum, and, though I am fearful to admit it, my own Temple.
I have told you what you need to know.

The Gardener believes that the destruction of the source will stop the disease. He is right. And wrong. To understand why, you must understand that the origin of this infection is mundane. Not long ago, an unknown force attacked and damaged the city. In the wake of its destruction, a small part of me was wounded. The wound itself was not serious, but like any wound left untreated, it soon became worse, and thus the infection started. And perhaps it would have ended, had not the Gardener intervened.
Again, thank you. A shame it had to die.
Thank you once again.

It just wandered back in this morning! No doubt you had something to do with it? Excellent! I knew I had a good feeling about you, and I was right! As promised, the reward, plus a little something extra. I think it appropriate given the nature of this little dwemeri excursion, no?
